s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly growing caruncular lesion with ulceration
salient_findings: Amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface
Solid tumor with anaplastic cells and mitotic activity
key_facts: 4-week history of a rapidly growing left caruncular lesion
Amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface
Lesion arose from the caruncle
No evidence of primary acquired melanosis (PAM)
Specimen measured 8 × 6 × 5 mm with a 4-mm ulceration
Necrotic tissue on the surface of the specimen
Solid tumor with an inflamed crust on its surface
Large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity
Positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A
Significant number of cycling cells shown by Ki-67 proliferation marker
Sentinel lymph node biopsy findings were negative
Conjunctival and orbital biopsies revealed no tumor

differentials: Myoepithelial carcinoma of the lacrimal gland
per_call: Myoepithelial carcinoma of the lacrimal gland

shortlist.label: Malignant melanoma of the caruncle
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly growing amelanotic mass with ulceration, positive reactivity to melanocytic markers

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Ulcerated lesion with rapid growth, although less likely given the specific markers

shortlist.label: Sebaceous gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location in the caruncle, a site with sebaceous glands, but less likely due to specific melanocytic markers

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the location and ulceration, but less likely due to the specific histopathological findings

shortlist.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid growth and ulceration, but less likely given the specific markers and location

raw.rationale: The lesion's rapid growth, amelanotic and pedunculated nature, ulcerated surface, and origin from the caruncle, combined with histopathological findings of large anaplastic cells, mitotic activity, and positive reactivity to melanocytic markers, strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Lack of specific markers and the presence of melanocytic markers make this less likely

rejected.label: Sebaceous gland carcinoma
rejected.why: No indication of sebaceous gland origin or specific markers for this type of cancer

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Typical basal cell carcinoma features, such as palisading nuclei, were not mentioned

rejected.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
rejected.why: No mention of neuroendocrine markers or features typical of Merkel cell carcinoma
